newsitem.title: INDIA: India sugar prices up sharply, strike hurt supplies.
newsitem.headline: India sugar prices up sharply, strike hurt supplies.

text.p: Indian sugar prices on Monday rose sharply on a shortage of stocks compounded by an ongoing truckers' strike, dealers said.
In the ready delivery sugar S-30 moved up by 60/75 rupees at 1,350/1,425 rupees per quintal while M-30 rose by 85/70 rupees at 1,425/1,450 rupees.
"Arrivals of sugar from mills to the market remained virtually absent on account of the ongoing nationwide strike by transport operators," one broker said.
Indian truckers are off the roads since April 1 to protest a service tax and hike in insurance premiums.

Dealers said sugar delivery from the wholesale market to retail counters were also affected. Some were taking bags of sugar from the wholesale market to retail counters in their own vehicle or in taxis, they said.
Sugar mill delivery rose marginally to 1,210/1,230 rupees per quintal from 1,200/1,220 rupees.
The Bombay sugar market will be closed on Tuesday for a local Hindu festival and will reopen for trading on Wednesday.
